ai-framework.overview:
The Next-Gen Enterprise Governance Framework is the Foundation's flagship governance initiative — a compliant, on-chain governance stack that productizes two independently developed primitives: the Aether governance kernel and the Havix network layer. The framework is engineered for a specific gap in the market. Traditional enterprises concentrate decision authority in shareholder meetings, leaving strategy disconnected from the customers and frontline employees who actually observe the market. At the other extreme, so-called "DAO" products in the wild typically run on a centralized database: voting tallies, membership rosters and even final results can be silently rewritten by a backend operator. Neither model gives participants verifiable, tamper-evident governance.

The framework resolves this by separating concerns across a layered architecture. The Aether kernel provides immutable governance primitives on Arbitrum — three-chamber councils, weighted voting, soulbound-identity ranks and a Safe multisig treasury — without issuing any token. The Havix network layer provides the off-chain coordination plane: a dual-plane P2P network where public governance signals are observable while private deliberation remains cryptographically unlinkable. Enterprise customers adopt both layers through a productized access form that maps their existing shareholders, brand-loyal customers, management and employees into a four-power checks-and-balances community.

The compliance posture is explicit and non-negotiable. The framework does not issue tokens, does not conduct public fundraising, and does not pool customer funds; all enterprise payments settle through onshore corporate bank accounts of a mainland operating entity, not through any on-chain treasury. A legal-entity backstop underwrites the entire system, and governance outputs on-chain are recorded as advisory opinions rather than binding corporate resolutions. Where regulator-facing surfaces are needed, the public plane is structured to be observable as an information-service platform; private deliberation is treated analogously to encrypted IM or email. These choices are deliberate compliance redundancy, not workarounds, and they are reflected in every layer below.
ai-framework.architecture:
Four-layer architecture, with a strict separation between on-chain immutability and off-chain coordination:

- Governance kernel layer (Aether, deployed on Arbitrum): Solidity 0.8.26 contracts audited and remediated, built on OpenZeppelin and Foundry. Three chambers — Council, Parliament and Elders — provide weighted voting (50% citizen weight + 50% three-chamber weight), impeachment (30% quorum + 70% support), fixed terms and a veto channel. A 14-rank soulbound-token (SBT) identity system encodes appointed and retired elders, citizen cooldown and dormancy handling. The kernel is tokenless, operated by a non-profit foundation under a Safe multisig, with a legal-entity backstop; the Treasury Transparency ledger records every donation.
- Network layer (Havix): a four-layer P2P stack with a critical dual-plane isolation. The public plane uses gossipsub mesh and KadDHT (for Wiki CIDs only) and is the surface a regulator can observe; the private plane uses SHA-256-named topics with AES-256-GCM re-encrypted payloads, analogous to encrypted IM. A single master DID derives four context sub-identities (A=public, B=market, C=tunnel, D=wiki) via HKDF-SHA256, and sub-identities are cryptographically unlinkable. The economic layer runs a Reputation (cumulative, non-transferable) ↔ Credit (consumable, transferable) dual ledger; issuing Credit requires freezing an equal amount of the issuer's Reputation.
- Bridge service layer: a "hash writer" operated by a mainland legal entity. It writes only the SHA-256 hash of each finalized governance resolution onto the Aether on-chain ledger. It does not touch funds, does not touch user data, and does not hold custody of any asset. The bridge is intentionally one-directional and minimal so that its operator can be audited as a pure information-service role.
- Enterprise access layer: the productized four-power checks-and-balances community — shareholders and capital (50%) plus brand citizens (50%), with an executive layer and employee sub-DAO. Layered permissions are absolutely isolated: shareholder-only matters are retained under company-law defaults; the 50/50 co-governance layer handles shared matters; the employee self-governance layer handles internal welfare; a neutral council tier acts as buffer. A 50/50 deadlock breaker is built in: council compromise → second referendum → single board adjudication, with citizen-qualification purging between rounds.
ai-framework.roadmap:
Current status: the Aether governance kernel v3.0 contracts have completed audit remediation (5 P0 + 15 P1 findings closed); the Havix network layer M10 validation form is complete with 1234/1234 tests passing (1021 MVP + 213 Embas translation-market). Both primitives are integration-ready.

Four-phase plan:

- Phase 1 (2026 H1): launch the first 100-enterprise free pilot cohort. Each pilot deploys privately inside the enterprise perimeter; the Aether on-chain contracts are deployed for governance-attestation purposes only. The bridge service is stood up and its mainland operating entity registered. No enterprise is charged during this phase.
- Phase 2 (2026 H2): ship the dynamic-weighting algorithm — consumption contribution 40% + activity 30% + credit 30% — paired with an anti-cheat behavior-graph detector that flags coordinated vote farming. A co-governance incentive pool is introduced to reward sustained participation, and an employee-load early-warning threshold is added so that governance fatigue is surfaced before it distorts quorum.
- Phase 3 (2027 H1): ZKP privacy upgrade — only aggregate governance results are stored on-chain, individual ballots remain off-chain and provable. The proxy-contract upgradeable architecture is rolled out, governed by a 3/5 multisig across five roles: development side, enterprise side, independent audit, legal counsel and a user representative. Liability isolation is formalized by spinning community operations into a subsidiary.
- Phase 4 (2027 H2): deep integration with enterprise OA/ERP systems, cluster-level sub-DAO federation for multi-subsidiary groups, and the Havix M13 Rust rewrite of credit/arbitration/identity/market/wiki with slot-based saturated cover-traffic protocol — enabling sovereign-boundary defense against observer attacks at production traffic volumes.
ai-framework.team:
The framework is jointly developed by the Aether Foundation governance team and Havix Contributors, operating under the same GitHub organization (eneatlnc-cell). The two teams contribute complementary halves: the governance kernel is authored by the Foundation's Solidity track, the network layer by the Havix P2P track, and the bridge service and enterprise access form are co-authored across both.

The development workflow follows an internal code-review process — commits carry change-tags such as C-4, H-9 and M-10 — and ships documentation in both Chinese and English, reflecting the cross-jurisdictional nature of the deployment: the on-chain kernel runs on Arbitrum, while the operating entity and the bridge service sit in mainland China. The codebase carries full audit reports per milestone, with P0/P1/P2 severity classifications, and a NEXT-STEPS.md maintains a multi-layer recursive structure for traceable decision-making. Parallel AI-agent-assisted audits are used as a second review channel and are explicitly acknowledged in the audit reports.

The commercial model is deliberately back-loaded. Phase 1 pilots are free; paid subscriptions and a transaction-share model are introduced only after two years and only after both year-on-year revenue uplift and pilot-completion metrics are demonstrated by the enterprise. OA/ERP integration and community-operations services are offered as optional add-ons rather than bundled into the base framework. This sequencing is enforced by the Foundation, not by the enterprise customer, to keep the framework's incentive structure aligned with long-term governance health rather than short-term onboarding volume.

Specific contributor names are not yet published. The Foundation will release a named roster once the Phase-1 100-enterprise pilot cohort is complete and the operating entity has cleared its compliance review — both conditions must be satisfied before individual contributors can be publicly associated with the framework.

video-protocol.overview:
The Video Player Protocol is the Foundation's flagship media-access initiative, implemented as an open-source Android client (codename Memento) that combines sing-box TUN-based cross-continent network access, yt-dlp search and direct-link resolution, and ExoPlayer playback into a single signed APK. It targets users in network regions where direct access to global video sources (YouTube, Vimeo, Dailymotion, Bilibili) is unreliable, and pairs a one-device-one-code offline license model with JWT-based session management.

The MVP is a working end-to-end client — not yet a formally specified protocol — and the Foundation is transparent that the word "protocol" in the current name refers to the architectural intent of extracting the client's transport and resolution layers into a publishable specification once the field deployment proves which optimizations are worth standardizing.
video-protocol.architecture:
Three-tier separation, strict by design:

- Android client (Kotlin, JVM 17, minSdk 23, targetSdk 34): ActivationActivity (device-bound license) → MainActivity (search) → PlayerActivity (landscape ExoPlayer). MyApp handles process-level init for Chaquopy (embedded Python 3.11 running yt-dlp), sing-box libbox (v1.13.14), Room, Retrofit, EncryptedSharedPreferences.
- Cloud VPS (Python FastAPI, stateless): POST /activate verifies HMAC activation codes with constant-time comparison and issues HS256 JWT (7-day TTL, jti recorded for per-token revocation); GET /resolve runs yt-dlp server-side and returns a direct media URL; GET /health for liveness. SQLite WAL stores activated_devices and issued_jtis. Rate-limited at 5/min and 30/min respectively.
- Local license tool (pure Python stdlib): generates XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX activation codes from HMAC-SHA256(SECRET, device_lock), no network access; SECRET is shared only between VPS env and the operator's machine, never bundled in the APK.

Device lock = SHA-256(ANDROID_ID + "|" + UUID), persisted in EncryptedSharedPreferences. SQLite (Room) is wrapped by SQLCipher 4.5.4 with a 32-byte random key stored in the Android Keystore. The sing-box TUN runs at MTU 9000 with auto_route and strict_route, VLESS+uTLS(chrome) outbound.
video-protocol.roadmap:
Current status: versionCode 1, versionName 1.0 — MVP fully functional across activation, search, playback, download, and VPN. Tested through Android 14 with FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_SPECIAL_USE handling.

Next milestones:

- Q1 2026: protocol specification v0.1 — formally document the activation flow, JWT jti revocation semantics, and the /resolve response shape so third-party clients can interoperate.
- Q2 2026: add adaptive bitrate (HLS/DASH) handling in PlayerActivity to reduce first-frame latency and recover from direct-link expiry without a full re-resolve round trip.
- Q3 2026: edge resolver deployment in three regions (US/EU/SG) with shared JWT issuer, eliminating the current single-point VPS bottleneck for cross-continent resolution latency.
- 2027: extract the sing-box + libbox integration as a reusable Foundation SDK so that other Foundation media initiatives can adopt the same transport layer without re-implementing it.
video-protocol.team: Developed under the Foundation's media research track with the codename Memento. The codebase shows evidence of an internal review process (commits carry tags such as C-4/C-5/C-6/H-1/H-9/H-10/M-10/M-14) and evolved from an earlier internal project codenamed Lumine (SingBoxManager.kt still carries migration notes). DEPLOYMENT.md and USER_GUIDE.md total ~900 lines and are written in Chinese with English technical terms. The maintainer labels itself simply as "memento.app" (applicationId); specific contributor names are not yet published. The Foundation will release a named roster alongside the Q1 2026 protocol specification.

self-organizing-net.overview:
The Decentralized Self-Organizing Network is the Foundation's flagship P2P overlay initiative, implemented as the open-source Havix protocol — a Haven of Affinity for high-cognition individuals. Havix is built to validate a sociological hypothesis: that a stratified, self-organizing network can sustain a parallel coordination space without relying on either centralized platforms or pure-anonymity overlays like Tor. Its three defining primitives are decentralized transport (libp2p + IPFS, no central servers), gated admission (4-context DID derivation + weighted vouch), and reputation-anchored economics (Reputation/Credit dual-ledger with frozen-credit Faucet).

The current milestone (M10) has the validation form complete: 1021 MVP tests + 213 Embas translation-market tests = 1234/1234 passing, with 5 P0 + 15 P1 audit findings all fixed. The network is in private internal beta pending M11 multi-app coexistence and weighted-transition rollout.
self-organizing-net.architecture:
Four-layer protocol stack, with a critical dual-plane isolation that distinguishes Havix from naive "encrypt everything" designs:

- Application layer (parasitic): Wiki SPA, Market SPA, private-message tunnels, CLI — all loaded as signed apps through the M9 AppManager with manifest-based permission whitelisting (28 permissions across 8 categories).
- Identity layer: a single master DID derives 4 context sub-identities (A=public, B=market, C=tunnel, D=wiki) via HKDF-SHA256; sub-identities are cryptographically unlinkable.
- Protocol layer (public + private): Vouch, Wiki, Market, Offer·Credit, Arbitration — split across a public plane (gossipsub mesh + KadDHT for Wiki CIDs only + Rendezvous) and a private plane (private gossipsub topics whose names are SHA-256 of invite tokens, message bodies AES-256-GCM re-encrypted with HKDF-derived keys).
- Economic layer: Reputation (cumulative, non-transferable) ↔ Credit (consumable, transferable) dual ledger; high-reputation nodes can issue Credit only by freezing an equal amount of their own Reputation, anchoring Credit value to the issuer's reputation.

The S-Node class is the local node instance: libp2p (TCP + noise + yamux/mplex + gossipsub + mDNS + KadDHT) + helia IPFS + 8 local ledgers (reputation, credit, vouch, wiki, arbitration, treasury, market, credit-nonces). Cross-node consistency is achieved via gossipsub message convergence.
self-organizing-net.roadmap:
Current milestone: M10 — translation market (Embas) end-to-end working, full-stack security hardening (M9.6 + AUDIT-M10) complete. Embas uses context-B only (deliberately avoiding context-A to preserve unlinkability) with minReputation=30 and trustWeight=0.8; the complete publish→accept→deliver→approve→dispute→arbitrate flow runs with 5-node ad-hoc arbitration panels (≥3 verdict majority) and slash distribution of 50% to victim + 50% to treasury.

Stage plan (four phases total):

- M1–M10 Validation form: ✅ complete (1234/1234 tests passing).
- M11–M12 Complete form: multi-app coexistence (teaching market + wiki app), FW-01 weighted-transition algorithm v0 (trustWeight = real-flow ratio × counterparty diversity × minReputation coefficient, with collusion detection via Herfindahl index), 6 node-level attack defenses (rate limiting, eclipse detection, collusion statistics, exit penalty, commit-reveal front-running defense, reverse audit).
- M13–M14 Network form: Rust reimplementation of credit/arbitration/identity/market/wiki (with lmdb/sled storage + rust-libp2p); slot-based saturated cover-traffic protocol for sovereign-boundary defense against observer attacks.
- M15+ Ecosystem form: multi-language SDK, cross-network federation, mobile node support.

Relay rotation: 20% probability per 1-hour epoch, top 30% reputation + ≥3 vouches required to serve as relay. Tunnel: 3 parallel relays, MAX_CHUNK_SIZE 64 KiB, hard-cut switching (no circuit migration). Self-healing verified in 4-node star topology — 90-second detection and re-convergence after forced center-node shutdown.
self-organizing-net.team: Havix is developed by "Havix Contributors" under the MIT license, with the GitHub organization eneatlnc-cell. The codebase is unusually well-documented for its maturity: the Technical Whitepaper v0.1.0-draft lists 18 explicit design decisions with rationale, M8/M9/M10 each have full audit reports with P0/P1/P2 severity classifications, and the NEXT-STEPS.md runs to a six-layer recursive structure (Layer 0–5) for traceable decision-making. The development workflow uses parallel AI-agent-assisted audits (explicitly acknowledged in AUDIT-M9 and AUDIT-M10). Comments and design docs are predominantly in Chinese with English technical identifiers. The Foundation expects the named maintainer roster to be published once M11 multi-app coexistence stabilizes.
